book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
author: John J. Murphy

rules.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
rules.author: John J. Murphy
rules.rule: Price can 'walk the band' during strong trends, staying near the upper band in an uptrend or near the lower band in a downtrend. Do not short just because price is at the upper band in a strong trend.

parameter_impact.description: Prevent short signals when price walks upper BB in uptrend

rules.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
rules.author: John J. Murphy
rules.rule: Bollinger Band squeeze (narrow bands) indicates low volatility and predicts an upcoming explosive move. The direction of the breakout determines the trade. A squeeze followed by a close outside the band is a high-probability signal.

parameter_impact.description: BB squeeze detection adds to entry score

rules.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
rules.author: John J. Murphy
rules.rule: A doji candle (open ≈ close) indicates indecision and potential trend reversal. At market extremes or after a long trend, doji signals exhaustion. Requires confirmation from the following candle before acting.

parameter_impact.description: Doji near extremes adds minor signal; needs next candle confirmation

rules.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
rules.author: John J. Murphy
rules.rule: A bullish engulfing pattern at a support level is a strong reversal signal. A bearish engulfing at resistance confirms selling pressure. The larger the engulfing candle relative to the prior candle, the stronger the signal.

parameter_impact.description: Engulfing pattern near key levels adds to entry score

rules.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
rules.author: John J. Murphy
rules.rule: A hammer at the bottom of a downtrend signals potential reversal. A shooting star at the top of an uptrend signals potential reversal. Long shadow shows rejection of the extreme price level.

parameter_impact.description: Hammer/Shooting star pattern detection

rules.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
rules.author: John J. Murphy
rules.rule: Do not concentrate all capital in a single market or a single trade. Diversify across uncorrelated markets to reduce portfolio risk. Position sizing should reflect the correlation between open positions.

parameter_impact.description: Portfolio-level diversification rule — reduces per-trade sizing when correlated positions exist

rules.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
rules.author: John J. Murphy
rules.rule: An uptrend is defined by a series of higher highs and higher lows. A downtrend is defined by lower highs and lower lows. Breaking this structure signals a potential reversal.

parameter_impact.description: Validate structural trend via HH/HL for long, LH/LL for short

rules.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
rules.author: John J. Murphy
rules.rule: Moving averages act as dynamic support and resistance. In a strong uptrend, pullbacks to the 20 or 50 MA offer low-risk entry points. In a downtrend, rallies to the MA offer short entry points.

parameter_impact.description: Pullback to MA in trend = high probability entry bonus

rules.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
rules.author: John J. Murphy
rules.rule: A bullish signal is generated when the shorter-period moving average crosses above the longer-period moving average (golden cross). A bearish signal is the opposite (death cross). The 50-day and 200-day MAs are the most widely watched.

parameter_impact.description: MA crossover adds to trending score

rules.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
rules.author: John J. Murphy
rules.rule: The MACD line crossing above the signal line is a buy signal. Crossing below is a sell signal. Histogram crossing zero line is an earlier but less reliable signal.

parameter_impact.description: MACD crossover is a core trend entry signal

rules.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
rules.author: John J. Murphy
rules.source_chapter: Chapter 13 - The Link Between Stocks and Bonds
rules.rule: Analysis should always begin with the longer timeframe to establish the primary trend, then move to shorter timeframes for entry timing. Never trade against the higher timeframe trend.

parameter_impact.description: Higher timeframe alignment is a mandatory entry filter (ENFORCE_MULTI_TIMEFRAME)

rules.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
rules.author: John J. Murphy
rules.rule: Oscillators are most useful in non-trending (ranging) markets. In strongly trending markets, overbought and oversold signals can be misleading. Always determine the market regime before relying on oscillator readings.

parameter_impact.description: Suppress oscillator-only signals in TRENDING regime; weight by regime

rules.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
rules.author: John J. Murphy
rules.rule: Price above the 200-day moving average indicates a long-term bullish bias. Price below the 200-day MA indicates a bearish bias. Only take longs above the 200 MA, only take shorts below it.

parameter_impact.description: Price vs EMA200 is a mandatory directional filter

rules.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
rules.author: John J. Murphy
rules.rule: A minimum reward-to-risk ratio of 3:1 should be targeted. If the potential reward is less than 3 times the risk, the trade should be avoided. This ensures profitable trading even with a 50% win rate.

parameter_impact.description: Minimum R:R filter before entry — Murphy suggests 3:1

rules.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
rules.author: John J. Murphy
rules.rule: Round numbers tend to act as significant support and resistance levels. Psychologically significant price levels (1000, 50000 etc.) attract concentration.

parameter_impact.description: Minor bonus when price near round number levels

rules.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
rules.author: John J. Murphy
rules.rule: Bearish divergence: price makes a new high but RSI makes a lower high — indicates weakening momentum and potential reversal. Bullish divergence: price makes a new low but RSI makes a higher low — indicates momentum recovery.

parameter_impact.description: Divergence between price and RSI is the strongest reversal warning

rules.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
rules.author: John J. Murphy
rules.rule: RSI above 70 signals overbought conditions (potential reversal or pause). RSI below 30 signals oversold conditions (potential bounce). In strong trends, overbought/oversold can persist — use divergence for better timing.

parameter_impact.description: RSI extreme zones add to ranging score

rules.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
rules.author: John J. Murphy
rules.rule: A buy signal is generated when the Stochastic %K crosses above %D below 20 (oversold). A sell signal when %K crosses below %D above 80 (overbought). Best used in ranging markets; less reliable in strong trends.

parameter_impact.description: Stochastic cross in extreme zone adds to ranging entry score

rules.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
rules.author: John J. Murphy
rules.rule: Every trade must have a pre-determined stop-loss before entry. The stop should be placed at a logical technical level (below support, above resistance). A trade without a stop is a gamble, not a trade.

parameter_impact.description: Mandatory stop-loss enforcement; ENFORCE_STRICT_SL

rules.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
rules.author: John J. Murphy
rules.rule: Once a support level is broken, it becomes a new resistance level. Once a resistance level is broken, it becomes new support. The more times a level is tested, the more significant it becomes.

parameter_impact.description: Near key S/R levels adds to entry score; role reversal confirms breakout

rules.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
rules.author: John J. Murphy
rules.rule: A trend in motion tends to continue until a clear reversal signal appears. Always trade in the direction of the primary trend.

parameter_impact.description: Refuse signals against the primary trend direction

rules.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
rules.author: John J. Murphy
rules.rule: A decisive break of a major trendline is one of the best early warning signals of a change in trend. The longer and more times the trendline was tested, the more significant the break.

parameter_impact.description: Trendline break adds +1 to score as reversal signal

rules.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
rules.author: John J. Murphy
rules.rule: A price breakout from a consolidation pattern is only valid if accompanied by a significant increase in volume (at least 1.5x average). A breakout on low volume is suspect and often fails.

parameter_impact.description: Breakout signals require volume spike filter

rules.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
rules.author: John J. Murphy
rules.rule: Volume should increase in the direction of the trend. In an uptrend, volume should be heavier on up days than on down days. Declining volume in the trend direction is a warning of weakening.

parameter_impact.description: Volume confirmation required for trend entry; REQUIRE_VOLUME_CONFIRM
